stem_book: A trolley is moving horizontally with a velocity of v m/s w.r.t. earth (this velocity stays v throughout). A man starts running in the direction of motion of trolley from one end of the trolley with a velocity 1.5v m/s w.r.t. the trolley. After reaching the opposite end, the man turns back and continues running with a velocity of 1.5v m/s w.r.t. trolley in the backward direction. If the length of the trolley is L, then the displacement of the man with respect to earth, measured as a function of time, will attain a maximum value of (a) 4L/3 (b) 2L/3 (c) 5L/3 (d) 1.5L
reason: Added the intended assumption that the trolley keeps velocity v.
work: forward: t = L/(1.5v), ground speed 2.5v ⇒ 2.5v·L/(1.5v) = 5L/3; on return ground velocity −0.5v so 5L/3 is the max
